summary.en: Implement a complete small-language lexer with longest operators, comments, EOF, and line-numbered recovery.
summary.bn: দীর্ঘ অপারেটর, কমেন্ট, ইনপুটের শেষ এবং লাইনসহ ভুলের তথ্য সামলে ছোট ভাষার লেক্সার বানাও।

notes: Implementations were run with Python 3.12.14 and use only the standard library.

examples.title: Assignment and arithmetic
examples.explanationHtml: The assignment occupies line 1 and the print expression occupies line 2. The final newline places EOF at 3:1.

examples.title: Longest operator and full names
examples.explanationHtml: printable remains ID at 1:1. EQ starts at 1:10 and consumes both equals signs. The integer and semicolon follow.

examples.title: Recover at a forbidden character
examples.explanationHtml: The @ character is reported at 2:7. Scanning then continues with integer 7 and the semicolon, preserving their later columns.

examples.title: Whole-line and trailing comments
examples.explanationHtml: The first comment contributes no tokens. The next code begins at line 2. Its trailing comment is also skipped, and line 3 begins normally.

practice.title: Count recognised token categories
practice.statementHtml: Read source until end of input using the documented language. Ignore ERROR and EOF. Print KIND count for each present category in alphabetical category order. For empty or comment-only input, print nothing.
hints: Reuse tokenisation and count only successful non-EOF records.

practice.title: Collect lexical diagnostics
practice.statementHtml: Read source until end of input. Print line:column followed by a space and Python repr of the bad character for every ERROR. End with errors N. Use the lexer rules and one-character tab columns.
hints: Filter ERROR records without stopping at the first one.

practice.title: A three-equals boundary
practice.statementHtml: Tokenise x===y; and give the start column of each token, including EOF.
hints: The longest valid operator is only two characters.
practice.answerHtml: ID x at 1:1, EQ == at 1:2, ASSIGN = at 1:4, ID y at 1:5, SEMI at 1:6, EOF at 1:7. The scanner does not invent a three-character operator.

practice.title: Comment at end of file
practice.statementHtml: For source //hi with no newline, list the tokens and EOF location.
hints: The comment consumes all four stored characters.
practice.answerHtml: No ordinary tokens are emitted. The four-character comment moves the column from 1 to 5. EOF is emitted at 1:5. No newline means the line remains 1.

practice.title: Lexical versus syntax failure
practice.statementHtml: Does the lexer reject print + ; as a malformed expression? Explain the next stage.
hints: Each visible spelling has an allowed category.
practice.answerHtml: The lexer emits PRINT, PLUS, SEMI, and EOF. These are valid tokens. A parser must report that plus has no suitable operand under the expression grammar.

practice.title: State a progress argument
practice.statementHtml: Show that the main scan cannot report @ forever at one offset.
hints: Inspect the error branch after its yield.
practice.answerHtml: After yielding ERROR, the resumed generator increments both offset and column, then continues. Thus the next iteration sees a later character. Every other loop branch also advances, and the loop exits at source length.

quiz.prompt: Why does the lexer read printable before keyword lookup?
quiz.explanation: A keyword prefix cannot defeat a longer identifier.
options: To turn every name into PRINT

quiz.explanation: Checking = first would split the valid two-character operator.
options: It always appears earlier in source
It is the longer overlapping token

quiz.prompt: What record is emitted once after scanning finishes?
quiz.explanation: EOF explicitly marks input completion at the final cursor.
options: A second copy of the last token

quiz.prompt: How are tabs counted in this implementation?
quiz.explanation: The lesson defines character columns rather than editor display widths.

quiz.prompt: What does the lexer do with an isolated slash?
options: Start a comment without a second slash
Delete the rest of the line

quiz.prompt: Which text is a semantic concern after tokenisation?
quiz.explanation: Declaration checks need name information beyond spelling.
options: Whether == has one or two equals
The start column of a lexeme
Use of a well-spelled but undeclared name

quiz.prompt: Why is this implementation not constant-memory overall?
quiz.explanation: The source occupies O(n) memory even if tokens are consumed lazily.
options: It reads the whole source into a string
A generator stores every past token automatically

quiz.prompt: Which category does exact keyword lookup give printable?
quiz.explanation: The full spelling printable is absent from the keyword dictionary.

quiz.prompt: Where is EOF after scanning two characters and a newline?
quiz.explanation: The newline moves to line 2 and resets the column.

quiz.prompt: How many ERROR characters does this progress loop report?
quiz.code:
source = "@@"
pos = 0
errors = 0
while pos < len(source):
    errors += 1
    pos += 1
print(errors)
quiz.explanation: Each iteration consumes one bad character, so both are reported once.

quiz.prompt: What happens to 12roll under the documented token contract?
quiz.explanation: The scanner ends a digit sequence before the following letter; grammar checks come later.

quiz.prompt: Why can a comment end at EOF without an error here?
quiz.explanation: A // comment runs to newline or end of input by the stated language rule.
options: EOF is always a newline character
Line comments do not require a closing delimiter
The scanner ignores its own bounds

keyPoints.bn: স্ক্যানারের প্রতিটি শাখাকে সামনে এগোতে বা থামতে হবে।

examQuestions.question: Design a lexer record and cursor update policy for the classroom language.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
The complete classroom lexer contract
CategorySpellingPriority or boundary rule
LET, PRINTExact names let and printRead a complete identifier before keyword lookup.
IDASCII letter or underscore, then ASCII letters, underscores, or digitsConsume all identifier characters.
INTOne or more ASCII digitsA sign is a separate operator.
EQ==Check before the shorter = operator.
ASSIGN, PLUS, MINUS, STAR, SLASH= + - * /A // prefix starts a comment instead of two slash tokens.
LPAREN, RPAREN, SEMI( ) ;Each consumes one character.
ERRORAny unsupported characterReport its location, consume it, and continue.
EOFNo source spellingEmitted once at the final cursor location.

Yield category, spelling, start line, and start column. Advance for every consumed character and emit EOF at the final position.

examQuestions.question: Explain longest matching, keyword lookup, and a progress invariant in the hand-written scanner.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Read identifiers completely, then look up reserved spellings. Check == before = and // before slash. Every branch advances the cursor or finishes; the error branch consumes one character. These choices prevent false keyword prefixes, split operators, and repeated diagnostics at the same offset.

examQuestions.question: Extend the lexer to decimal literals while keeping a lone dot invalid. Describe the lookahead before consuming a dot.
examQuestions.answerHtml: After initial digits, consume a dot only if a following character exists and is an ASCII digit. Then consume all following digits. A dot without that evidence remains an unsupported character for the next scan iteration. This preserves progress and the stated requirement for digits after a decimal point.
